paper.title_en: Sourcing vector perturbations in warm inflation through shear viscous effects
paper.abstract_en: Vector modes are generally believed not to play a significant role in standard cosmological perturbation theory because they decay rapidly. Non-equilibrium dynamics in the radiation bath present during warm inflation can lead to shear viscous effects, requiring a description beyond the perfect-fluid approximation. We adopt the fluctuating hydrodynamic approach to account for stochastic anisotropic stress related to shear viscosity. We show that the vector mode obeys a constrained Langevin equation in an inflationary background. The resulting power spectrum, considered in the weak-viscosity regime, is proportional to the shear viscosity and it also depends on the Hubble slow-roll parameter $ε$, decaying approximately as $a^{-(1-ε)}$. This behaviour is significantly slower than the unsourced, non-viscous power spectrum, which decays as $a^{-4}$. The continuously sourced vector modes, nevertheless, decay on superhorizon scales, and the illustrative benchmark parameter choices adopted in our numerical examples give a negligible late-time vector-to-scalar ratio. Despite the absence of direct large-scale observable vector signatures, the main results establish a source of vector perturbations during warm inflation and provide a framework for studying possible secondary effects along with large-scale white noises in the vector channel.
